summary: Shigeru Gorai worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1929–1932) and Kyoto University (~1936–1939), later holding posts at Koyasan University, Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the Institute of Japanese Religious Folklore.
Shigeru Kato specialized in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1903 to ~1906 and later held a post there from ~1925 to ~1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1957) and Harvard University (~1961–1967). He held academic posts at the University of the Sacred Heart and Tenri University.

Shih Hu worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cornell, Columbia under John Dewey, National University, and under Kaiten Nukariya. His career included serving as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and leading Academia Sinica (1957–1962).
Shih-Hsiang Chen was a Sinologist who studied at Peking University from ~1932 to ~1936. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1945 to 1971.
Shikazo Mori specialized in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1927 to ~1930 and held a post at Bukkyo University from ~1970 to ~1979.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang in 1920. He held posts at Boone University (~1920–1922), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1947–1949).

Shimin Geng was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from ~1949 to ~1953 and held a post there from ~1953 to 2000.

Shin Fujinaga works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested in 1991, and as associate professor in 2000) and at Hiroshima University (attested in 1992).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the Third Higher School and Kyoto University under Kitarō Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto University (1935–1953), Kyoto City University of Arts, and Harvard.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and held a professorship at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College (attested in 2015).

Shin'ya Yasutomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1963–1967) and Otani University. He served as professor at Otani University in 2014 and held posts at the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies and the Eastern Buddhist Society.
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1934). He later held professorships at Taisho University (~1957–1978) and Hanazono University.

Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano, and held posts at Koyasan University as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1980–1986). He held posts at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1986–1989) and the University of Tokyo (~1989–2013).

Shinichi Nakazawa works in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977) and held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and the Australian National University under J.W. de Jong and A.L. Basham, later holding posts at Eastern Institute and ICPBS.

Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University from ~1984 to ~1993. He held a post at Tottori University (~1994–2000) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2006).

Shinjo Hinonishi specialized in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Shigeru Gorai and held posts at Koyasan University as assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and numerous other teachers, also studying with Tibetan masters. He held posts at the University at Buffalo (~1964–1966) and Toyo Bunko (~1966–1975).
